parts.visual:
A fundamental truth of corporate finance: Money is a product, and it has a price. That price is called the 'Cost of Capital'.

The Two Types of Money:
1. Debt (Bonds/Loans): Cheaper, but highly risky. If you miss a payment, the bank takes the company.
2. Equity (Stock): Safer, but highly expensive. You don't have to pay it back, but you give away permanent ownership and future profits.
parts.audio: Money is not free; it has a price called the Cost of Capital. Executives must choose between the cheap risk of Debt and the expensive safety of Equity.

questions.question: Your company needs $100 Million to build a new factory. Why might the CFO prefer to borrow the money (Debt) rather than sell new shares of stock (Equity)?
options: Because debt is mathematically cheaper. The interest payments are tax-deductible, and you don't dilute the ownership of the current shareholders.
questions.correct_answer: Because debt is mathematically cheaper. The interest payments are tax-deductible, and you don't dilute the ownership of the current shareholders.
questions.explanation: However, if the factory fails and you cannot make the interest payments, the bank will force you into bankruptcy.

questions.question: Listen to the CEO's dilemma. What financial danger is she facing?
questions.tts_text: Interest rates just doubled. We can no longer afford to borrow money to fund our expansion. We have to halt all construction.
options: A drop in the Cost of Capital.
A spike in the Cost of Capital (Macroeconomic Risk).
questions.correct_answer: A spike in the Cost of Capital (Macroeconomic Risk).
questions.explanation: When central banks raise interest rates, borrowing money becomes too expensive, forcing companies to shrink instead of grow.

questions.question: What does WACC stand for in corporate finance?
options: Weighted Average Cost of Capital. It is the average rate a company pays to finance its assets, blending both debt and equity.
questions.correct_answer: Weighted Average Cost of Capital. It is the average rate a company pays to finance its assets, blending both debt and equity.
questions.explanation: If a CEO pitches a new project that makes a 5% return, but the company's WACC is 8%, the project will actively destroy value.

questions.question: Why do startups almost exclusively use Equity (Venture Capital) instead of Debt (Bank Loans)?
options: Because startups burn cash and have no profits to make monthly interest payments. Banks won't lend to them, so they must sell ownership to survive.
questions.correct_answer: Because startups burn cash and have no profits to make monthly interest payments. Banks won't lend to them, so they must sell ownership to survive.
questions.explanation: Equity is the most expensive money in the world (giving up 20% of your company), but for a startup, it is the only money available.
